title: Post-canary observations and metrics playbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight playbook and meeting note for the first 48h after a canary roll (hosted/dedicated). Focus: what to check, quick queries, observed deviations, and decision criteria for rollforward/rollback or hotfix. This is intentionally tactical — use the Confluence runbook for the canonical checklist.

Meeting snapshot:
- Date: 2025-11-19 09:30 PT
- Duration: 30m
- Attendees: Marisol (release lead), Liam (SRE), Sana (serving-runtime), Jonah (telemetry), Priya (oncall eng)
- Channel: #release-control (Slack) thread pinned message at 09:22

Top-level summary:
- Canary completed at 03:14 PT with 10% traffic for 6h window. Initial smoke OK.
- Around 02:00–04:00 UTC we saw a small bump in backend 5xx tied to a rare timeout pattern (0.6% -> 1.8% p95). No user-facing outage; error budget within tolerance.
- Latency: p50 unchanged, p95 increased from 320ms -> 410ms for token-gen route. CPU on gpu-pool-03 spiked but recovered.
- No data corruption or KV cache mismatch detected.

Immediate observations (raw):
- PromQL (use in Grafana explore):
  - rate(http_requests_total{route="/v1/generate",env="canary"}[5m]) by (status)
  - histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket{route="/v1/generate",env="canary"}[5m])) by (le))
- Notable alerts fired: canary-high-5xx (threshold 1.5%) at 02:12 UTC — auto-ack by runbook, pager suppressed scope.
- Trace sample: request id f3a2... shows repeated kernel-schedule wait at step attention_kernel. Investigating kernel selection fallback in runtime.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel fallback path (quantized kernel) under certain seq-len combos is slower and times out under synthetic bursts. (Sana)
2) Autoscaler over-reacted to short-lived spike, briefly shifting replicas and introducing cold-start latency. (Liam)
3) Upstream dependency (redis shard) experienced GC that added 50–200ms p95 to cache fills. (Jonah)

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Sana: reproduce the attention_kernel trace locally with seq=1024 synthetic load. Add one more trace capture instrumentation. ETA: 2025-11-20 EOD.
- Liam: verify scaler logs and pod lifecycle events for gpu-pool-03 between 01:45–03:00 UTC; correlate with node metrics. ETA: 2025-11-19 16:00 PT.
- Jonah: capture histogram of redis latency and p99 for the canary cohort; check shard-7 metrics. ETA: 2025-11-19 15:00 PT.
- Marisol: prepare rollback criteria note (below) and schedule check-in at 18:00 PT.

Rollback / Rollforward decision criteria (quick):
- Immediate rollback if: 5xx > 3% sustained for 10m OR p95 latency > 2x baseline sustained for 15m AND customer-impact traces present.
- Graceful rollforward if: 5xx between 1.5–3% but root cause identified + mitigation (eg config change, retry backoff) with canary patch within 6h.
- Hotfix cadence: if fix requires runtime binary, prefer build+canary within 24h; if config, prefer immediate partial config push with 1% test traffic followed by 10% after 30m.

Manual verifications to run before any change:
- Run smoke script: ./tools/post_canary_smoke.sh --env canary --routes /v1/generate,/v1/embeddings (exit 0 expected for 50 random samples).
- Verify KV cache consistency: curl -H "x-test-cohort: canary" https://internal-api/kv/consistency-check
- Confirm no increase in user-facing errors in logs (search: "user_error" tag in last 60m).

Notes to oncall / next 24h watchlist:
- Watch canary-high-5xx, canary-latency-p95-alert, gpu-pool-03-cpu-surge.
- If autoscaler shows >2 scale events in 10m for pool-03, pin traffic to other pools and engage platform-engineering.
- Keep a rolling 10-min trace sample window; add extra verbosity for attention_kernel for next 6h.

Follow-ups for engineering tickets:
- RE-8742: Investigate kernel fallback perf and add micro-benchmarks (assigned Sana).
- RE-8743: Autoscaler retrospective — investigate hysteresis and dampening (assigned Liam).
- RE-8744: Redis shard GC tuning (assigned Jonah).

Retrospective prompts (collect before next weekly release sync):
- Which metric(s) gave the earliest signal for this regression? (was it 5xx, p95, tail IO?)
- Were there false positives from noise in the canary cohort? Can we refine cohort split?
- Does the autoscaler need different dampening for short synthetic bursts vs sustained load?

Unresolved questions / open items:
- Is the attention_kernel slowdown correlated with specific model versions or quantization profile? (need cross-check against model build metadata).
- Should we run an internal smoke with seq-length sweep (128 -> 2048) in staging nightly? (Sana/serving to propose schedule)

Appendix (quick links and commands):
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/xyz/canary-summary?orgId=1
- Traces search: http://jaeger.redwood.ai/search?service=serving-runtime&tag=canary
- Quick kubectl: kubectl -n gpu get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp --field-selector involvedObject.name=gpu-pool-03

End notes: this doc is a working log. Copy to Confluence with the tag "post-canary" when we have closure on RE-8742/8743/8744. If rollback is executed, update the top summary line with time and reason.

-- Marisol (release lead)
